chapter: Louis Armstrong, King Oliver and St. Louis memories
title: Armstrong plays Rockin' Chair; the spilled malted milk
summary: In his new suit, Thomas had a malted milk spilled on him while Armstrong, with Floyd Campbell's band, sang Rockin' Chair and silenced the room before the house erupted.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Bit about your impressions on this occasion when you heard Louis.

... so I got the suit and I think it was Hart, Shaffner and Marx, you know. And they served malted milks. In fact, if you wanted malted milks, some whiskey, if you wanted coffee sandwiches, delicious club sandwiches. ... so I'm trying to figure what to order and I wasn't doing any drinking. I was a

kid. I must have around 18 at that time. So I ordered a malted milk. And a cat comes to me and stumbles over my foot and spills the malted milk all down on my new suit. He says, I'm sorry and I say, I'm sorry, too, but nothing you can do about it. So in the meantime Pops is playing a tune. I never heard this tune before. And ... to hear from so when she comes in (singing) everybody is sitting around (more singing) ... trumpet now. What's he talking about? I just left him before. What's he talking about now? (singing) ... so the people must have felt the same way. It's a dancing or listening audience. You could dance or listen and a cat got up and he got this chick and he walks up to the front to dance (singing). They used to play these things, you know. After it was Floyd Campbells band, I think.
Oh, I was going to ask who he was playing with.
Floyd Campbell. I think it was Floyd Campbell's band
'Rocking Chair.' And I thought I sounded better ...
I know, I know. Don't you do this? I mean I know tunes but I mean I'm surprised how often nowadays I can't remember the names. I know the tunes.

And Stanley and Baby, everybody walked up to the bandstand and this cat is singing and playing. And, after he finished, I think it happens with anybody who is a performer, it's got to happen to you. It's got to happen to everybody

who performs and you think you've given all you've got. But, there's a split second, there's a complete silence that nothing happens. Nobody is dancing, people listening, just swing. So pretty soon, the whole house came down.
